correctness.rationale: The deterministic cycle identity |S triangle T|=|M-1| or M+1 proves a universal pointwise lower bound. Rotational invariance and an equivariant missing-edge deletion rule yield a uniform UST marginal, achieving it. The exact run-count distribution is derived from cyclic compositions and independently checked exhaustively for \(3\le n\le10\) and four rational biases. Indicator covariances give E M=npq and Var M=\(npq(1-3pq)\). The fixed-p CLT follows from stationary 1-dependence; the rare-bias Poisson law follows from a binomial limit and an O(np_n^2) adjacency error. originality.rationale: Theorem 1 and Section 3.1 of Mészáros–Peled (arXiv:2610.11554v1) prove a general minimum-degree bound via entropy and Marton coupling, not the sharp optimal transport on a cycle, its stochastic-minimality construction, the full optimal cost law, or the \(p_n\sim\lambda/n\) crossover. The circular-run probability formula and its Poisson asymptotics are credited to prior circular-run literature and are not presented as independently new. The Albin et al. tree-overlap problem minimizes overlap of two iid spanning trees over a variable law rather than coupling a prescribed one-out law to a uniform tree. No direct research record or published comparison implies the stated package. Independent priority checks could still identify a broader preexisting equivariant coupling theorem.
residual_risks: A preexisting group-equivariant optimal coupling principle or unindexed transport result may subsume the general rotation-invariant statement.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 UST versus 1-out theorem leaves the sparse-degree cycle benchmark with only a qualitative big-O bound. This result computes the sharp Wasserstein optimum, a coupling attaining it for all monotone edge-distance penalties, an explicit complete finite-size cost distribution, and a Poisson/Gaussian crossover including exact-match probability at rare bias. The statement is motivated by optimal transport of random spanning graphs and not merely by new notation or an isolated numeric instance. Known circular run counting is openly credited as a supporting ingredient.
